subject: Streaming chat latency spikes during peak test - customer escalation
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@nimbleretail.com>
To: support@nimbleretail.com, rishi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Streaming chat latency spikes during peak test

Hi team,

We ran a scheduled peak-traffic simulation this morning (concurrent users ~22k, burst to 30k) hitting the hosted streaming chat endpoint (SSE). Around 09:50 PDT we saw p95 latency jump from ~180ms to 1.6s and p99 climb to 4.8s for a sustained ~12 minute window. We also observed an uptick in 5xx error rate (0.2% -> 1.8%). Attached are a small set of request traces and a short video of the client behavior.

This is impacting our prototype checkout flow in the test environment; we need confirmation on root cause, an ETA for mitigation, and whether this will affect our production load test scheduled next week.

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Director, Platform Engineering
NimbleRetail

[attachments: request_traces_20270422.zip, customer_screenshots.png]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Streaming chat latency spikes during peak test

Forwarding NimbleRetail report — they hit a synthetic peak and saw sustained p95/p99 regressions + elevated 5xxs on streaming (SSE). They included request traces.

Quick context: hosted-api streaming path (chat.stream endpoint) started degrading under a burst test that looks like a mix of long-tail token generation and many short requests. Marcus/aditya — can you triage resource contention (KV cache, batching behavior, kernel selection) and share immediate mitigations? Laura — heads up this is a priority escalation with exec CC.

Key asks:
- Short-term mitigation to reduce customer impact (rolling traffic, model fallback, scale up)
- Preliminary cause hypothesis and what telemetry we need from the customer traces
- Communication draft for customer and execs (I can send)

Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: rishi@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Streaming chat latency spikes during peak test

Thanks for flagging. Quick triage notes after a rapid pass on traces:
- Traces show sustained KV cache misses during the spike window; many requests include slightly different prefixes so batching loss + cache churn looks likely.
- We see increased GPU kernel switch rate for long context lengths — that can push a fraction of requests into the slower execution path.
- Error rate correlates with transient quota exceeded errors from the serving frontends (burst queue overflow).

Immediate mitigations we can apply (15-30m):
1) Enable degraded-model fallback for streaming for this account only (route to the lower-latency quantized variant) — reduces per-token latency at cost of small quality delta.
2) Temporarily increase per-region streaming pool capacity by 20% (provision burst nodes) and lift the soft concurrency cap for the account.
3) Tighten prefix-aware batching window to reduce batch fragmentation for short requests.
4) Apply circuit-breaker to drop exceedingly large contexts at the frontend (return 429) to protect tail.

We'll prepare a quick runbook for the steps and execute in this order unless objections. Also will capture additional telemetry (KV hit rate, batch sizes, kernel path counts) and push traces to the shared drive link.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: rishi@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T12:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Streaming chat latency spikes during peak test

Looping in the customer-facing context: Sarah called our support line and escalated to their VP of Product. They are extremely worried about next week's production load test.

Ask from CS:
- Can we commit to a mitigation window and a follow-up post-mortem? Customer wants a short-term SLA (reduce p99 to <1s for their workload) for the upcoming test.
- If mitigation impacts quality, they want to understand the delta; please prepare an A/B sample comparison for the degraded variant.

Evelyn — flagging for awareness. If the mitigation requires cross-org credits or an SLA exception (dedicated pool for one-off load), we may need a quick exec sign-off.

I will draft the customer note once we have the exact mitigation plan and ETA.

Laura
Account Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@nimbleretail.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming chat latency spikes during peak test — immediate actions and next steps

Hi Sarah — thank you again for the traces and for flagging this quickly. We own this and wanted to summarize immediate actions and what to expect in the next 24 hours: 

What we are doing now (live):
- Routing your streaming traffic to a lower-latency quantized model variant for the remainder of today to reduce p95/p99 tail. Expect p95 ~200-350ms and p99 < 1s for the same workload.
- Provisioned +20% regional burst capacity and temporarily raised your soft concurrency cap to reduce queue overflows.
- Enabled a short frontend circuit-breaker for contexts > 2000 tokens to protect overall tail; requests above that threshold will receive 429 and a typed error with guidance.
- Collected additional telemetry (KV cache hit/miss, batch sizes, kernel path) and uploaded the traces to this folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Nimble-Retail-traces

Next steps (24-72h):
- Marcus & team will analyze kernel path switching and batching behavior and propose longer-term fix (kv-cache tuning + smarter prefix-aware batching).
- We'll produce an A/B quality comparison between your current model and the degraded variant and share sample outputs.
- CS will coordinate an internal readout and a follow-up post-mortem with root cause and mitigation roadmap.

If you'd like us to postpone your production load test until we've completed the analysis, we can do that — happy to coordinate timing.

We will provide an interim update in 3 hours and a full write-up within 48 hours. Apologies for the disruption; we know this is high priority.

Attachments: initial_mau_report.csv (summary), request_traces_20270422.zip

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Note to internal team: Laura, Marcus, Aditya — please assemble the post-mortem template and an exec one-pager we can send to Evelyn and Nimble's leadership. If any credit/waiver is required, loop Finance but let's keep that parallel.
